highlights.title: Sega Once Floated Cancelling Sonic the Hedgehog, but the Movies Changed Everything
highlights.summary: 2026 marks the 35th anniversary of the Sonic franchise, an impressive milestone for one of gaming's most iconic mascots. Though the series has had its ups and downs, and at one point that almost meant cancellation.
body: Reflecting on the series in a conversation with the press (as reported by One More Game ), Iizuka revealed that "during the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise." In response, Iizuka had to "fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible." While he doesn't give details on when Sega was floating cancellation or how long that period lasted, It is only in recent years that the series has regained momentum.

Iizuka noted that the biggest success for the franchise was the release of the first movie in 2020. Despite early backlash to Sonic's original design, the film was eventually released to massive box-office success. This showed Sega that there was still interest in the series while also helping to introduce a new generation of fans to the character. It "changed the course of this franchise," said Iizuka.

highlights.title: Lionel Richie Undergoes Heart Procedure, ‘Will Be Back on Stage Soon’ After Canceling Next Three Shows
highlights.summary: Lionel Richie will miss at least a few concert dates after being hospitalized this week and undergoing a procedure to treat atrial fibrillation, the singer’s rep says. “Lionel underwent a common procedure for Atrial fibrillation (AFib),” Richie’s representative said in a statement given to Variety.
body: The next three dates on the tour Richie has been on with Earth, Wind & Fire have been canceled. Those dates were scheduled for Saturday night in San Francisco, Sept. 30 in Chicago and Oct. 2 in Columbus, Ohio. The next shows on Richie’s concert calendar, a three-night stand at Las Vegas’ Encore Theater beginning Oct. 14, are still on, as of this writing.

The Mayo Clinic describes the common AFib procedure as “treatment for an irregular and often very fast heartbeat… The treatment uses heat energy, cold energy or high-energy electric pulses to create tiny scars in an area of the heart. The signals that tell the heart to beat can’t pass through scar tissue. So the treatment helps block faulty signals that cause AFib.”
Richie’s health has been in the news lately with some other canceled dates and hospitalizations, although he has seemingly quickly bounced back in each instance.

On June 24, on the first night of the joint tour with EWF, the singer brought a show in Minneapolis to an early halt after mentioning feeling dizzy, and he subsequently canceled two dates, but he was back on stage for the tour’s June 30 stop, and told the crowd not to worry.

highlights.title: Shuffling the deck chairs: Xbox continues its "reset" with dramatic restructuring
highlights.summary: When Xbox announced sweeping layoffs in July as part of a brutal "reset" for the gaming brand, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said part of the pre-existing problem in the gaming unit was "teams, studios, and functions [that] often operate independently, [making it] harder to work toward a shared goal."…
body: The biggest apparent change is for the Halo franchise, which will now be under the remit of Call of Duty maker Activision. Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries), which recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved, will remain as just a “small team” to support the player community, Microsoft said, with the remaining staffing roles eliminated as part of 268 newly announced layoffs.

“For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision President Rob Kostich said in a statement provided to Kotaku. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.”
Activision, which Microsoft officially purchased just under three years ago, will now also take control of venerable studio Rare ( Sea of Thieves ) and the Age of Empires stewards at World’s Edge.

highlights.title: Viture’s Vonder Glasses Are Meant to Map Your Mind
highlights.summary: No cameras? No problem. Viture’s first display-free smart glasses have bone-conduction microphones to privately record your daily musings.
body: David Jiang, cofounder and CEO of smart glasses company Viture, tells me about how he used to yell at his kid.

His 10-year-old son played tennis. During tournaments, Jiang says he had a habit of shouting and criticizing his son’s mistakes as he played. He wanted to apply pressure to make him succeed—it was the way he’d been taught to raise kids, after all. It made sense.

But then, unprompted, his smart glasses sent him a message. The AI assistant in his company’s newest wearable had picked up on what he was doing, recognized that his behavior wasn’t helpful, and messaged him about what he should do differently. Stop shouting. Stop criticizing. Just be there, be present, and show that you support your son. That worked, Jiang says, and being called out like that has supposedly made him a better father and improved the relationship with his kid, all thanks to his yet-to-be-released Vonder AI glasses.
“I didn't know this until Vonder could find my pattern,” Jiang says. “This is not only a tool that can summarize your life, but also a tool that can help yourself to be a better person.”

highlights.title: Xbox’s Forza Studios Have Been Tag-Teaming For Years. Now They’re Becoming One
highlights.summary: Big changes are afoot at Microsoft, as the company announced a massive reorganization of its Xbox gaming division. While Activision and Bethesda will expand their remit, adding several studios to their portfolio, Forza series developers Playground and Turn 10 won't be included in the consolidation.
body: "These two studios have been creative and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team," Xbox chief creative officer Matt Booty wrote in a letter to employees. What the letter doesn't precisely mention is if there'll be layoffs at these studios, but we do know that 268 positions at Xbox are being made redundant as part of a previously announced second wave of job cuts. Mergers typically see several roles overlap, so it won't be too surprising to see people let go from both studios as they start the process of becoming a single team.

Playground Games has a storied career, having developed the first Forza Horizon game, released in 2012. Since then, the studio has developed each entry in the franchise, which slowly overtook the main Forza Motorsport series to become one of Xbox's tentpole franchises. Forza Horizon 6 was released earlier this year to positive reviews, and next year will bring a new chapter in the Fable series. Turn 10 Studios is an even older developer, having been established in 2001 to develop racing games for Microsoft Game Studios.

highlights.title: Meta patches Muse exploit that let attackers control the AI agent
highlights.summary: Meta has issued a patch for its Muse macOS app following the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability that could allow someone to take control of the AI agent. The bug found by security researcher Patrick Wardle utilized an undocumented Muse setting that enabled potential attackers running local code…
body: ‘They should be thinking about security from the very start, and they are just not.’

Several design decisions reportedly enabled this flaw, including having Muse dictation occur in the cloud instead of on-device, and allowing any app to control all of Muse’s undocumented settings. Proof-of-concept attacks developed by Wardle to test the exploit enabled him to take pictures and write malicious files to disk via Muse, which did not alert the user in many cases.

“We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want. So instead of us having to write a very comprehensive Mac malware stealer, we can just leverage the AI assistant itself,” Wardle told Ars Technica. “At the very least, they should be thinking about security from the very start, and they are just not.”

That stands in contrast with the emphasis that Meta placed on Muse’s privacy and security features when it announced the AI agent earlier this month. Meta patched the vulnerability in the hours following the Ars report being published, and asserts that real-world security concerns were minimal because the exploit required local access to the user’s device.

highlights.title: Bloodborne’s JackSepticEye Says He’s A “Vibe-Checker” For The Movie
highlights.summary: When the R-rated Bloodborne movie was officially announced with YouTuber Seán McLoughlin AKA JackSepticEye signed on as a producer, many wondered what, exactly, his involvement might be. Now, we have a better idea.
body: Appearing on 100 Questions with Tom Simons ( via GamesRadar ), McLoughlin said you can think of his role as a producer as a "vibe-checker" for the movie. In essence, McLoughlin said that when he's on calls with stakeholders discussing key elements of the "vetting process" and hiring, he speaks up and helps make decisions.

He went on to say that he's not trying to shepherd the Bloodborne movie to become "the game," or a movie that tries to "one up the game" or compete with it. Instead, McLoughlin said his ambition is to "honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

Before this, McLoughlin said he's not trying to make a quick buck with the Bloodborne movie, though if the movie is a success, it stands to reason that he would participate in that given his status as a producer. He has spoken about his extreme passion for the franchise, saying he believes working on the Bloodborne movie is what he was put on this Earth to do.
Bloodborne is not the only From Software game getting a film adaptation, as a live-action Elden Ring is on the way from director Alex Garland and A24.

highlights.title: Supermarket roast chicken taste test: ‘Ham-flavoured chook is extremely divisive’
highlights.summary: In a bid to establish a pecking order of eight roast chooks, Nicholas Jordan samples a ‘truly neutral’ chicken and another that triggers feelings of dismay. If you value our independent journalism, we hope you’ll consider supporting us today.
body: I would guess that over the course of my childhood, 50% of all large family events featured a roast chicken. I have no idea where the chickens came from, but I know it wasn’t from our oven. Sometimes these chickens tasted as if they were baked under the care of Stephanie Alexander. Other times they had the moisture content of an Ugg boot and tasted as though they’d been seasoned by fourth-century ascetic monks. I may be exaggerating the facts here, but not my feelings.

I have since developed a deep and multifaceted interest in poultry, and was thrilled at the thought of eating eight supermarket roast chickens. Imagine your boss saying: “Don’t worry about the report, I’d rather you spend the afternoon finding deeper ways to engage in your hobby.” I wasn’t the only one – the last time there was this much interest in joining a taste test was when we tried chocolate.

Note: we also tasted Hazeldenes Free Range Sourdough BBQ Chicken (available in Harris Farm stores in Sydney) as a point of comparison. It was both the most divisive and highest-scoring chicken, mostly due to it tasting far saltier than any other chicken.

highlights.title: Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype
highlights.summary: It’s been a busy few months for AI hype. At the end of April, Anthropic claimed that its model Claude Mythos is better at finding software vulnerabilities than most security experts.
body: This was followed by Anthropic ’s claim that one of its models had made a mathematical breakthrough; soon OpenAI claimed a mathematical breakthrough of its own. Most recently, Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon went viral announcing his departure from the company, claiming that it and OpenAI are “racing straight towards self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”

Each of these events was mostly covered breathlessly by the press, often repeating the companies’ anthropomorphizing framings —which are designed to portray their software is not only powerful but incipient “ artificial general intelligence.” So what is really going on? Are we witnessing a massive, civilization-changing set of technological breakthroughs, or is this marketing?

In all these incidents, massive fanfare from the companies (presented as mea culpas in illicit hacking cases) is accompanied by intense press coverage. Once there is time for experts in the relevant fields to examine what happened, a very different story emerges, but one that gets less media attention.

body: Assuming this teaser plays out like other recent LEGO announcements, we can expect to see details of LEGO’s upcoming Dragon Ball set(s) in the coming weeks.

For now, there’s no word on any specific Dragon Ball sets or release dates. The furthest-out release date for any announced LEGO sets is January 1, which is when the LEGO Super Mario minifigure sets will hit store shelves (some of those sets are available for preorder now).
Dragon Ball was created by Akira Toriyama as an anime TV series that ran from 1986 - 1989 in Japan. It has since turned into a whole franchise of additional TV series, movies, video games, and more.

LEGO’s teaser shows six Dragon Balls, yellow-orange spheres with varying numbers of red stars on them. While six Dragon Balls together have no special power, introducing the seventh makes them able to summon their Eternal Dragon, who can grant wishes. That’s what’s implied when the seventh ball rolls in during the teaser video, right before it ends.

highlights.title: Great to see what Tom Cruise’s belly button looks like, but it’s the stuff he is never asked about that interests me | Marina Hyde
highlights.summary: Most stars, and especially women, are endlessly expected to explain the past: the lessons learned and all the regrets. But not Tom – it’s Hollywood’s free pass. There really is no press tour like a Tom Cruise press tour – which is why there have not really been any Tom Cruise press tours for a very…
body: At some level, you have to admire the mad image-industrial complex that labours to keep “the last movie star” from having to talk about the things all the other movie stars are required to lay on the line in order to promote their wares. Only a few weeks ago, Kidman was on the cover of Vogue being required to pick over her two marriages in what was otherwise the most saccharine of interviews.

Meanwhile, the world is obliged on pain of death to regard the 64-year-old Tom Cruise as ageless (and probably deathless). A few years ago, his Top Gun co-star Kelly McGillis – 62 at the time – explained why she had not been approached to return for the sequel, Top Gun Maverick. “I’m old and I’m fat, and I look age-appropriate for what my age is,” she replied with deadly affectlessness, “and that is not what that whole scene is about.”

highlights.title: A New Tool Found Malware That’s Guided by an AI Hive Mind—No Humans in Sight
highlights.summary: Cisco Talos researchers created a new framework for identifying malware and hacking tools that rely on AI chatbots—and quickly discovered something unusual.
body: For years, cybersecurity practitioners have tracked different types of malware and detected potential infections using digital fingerprints to identify different hacking tools and follow their use over time. As attackers are increasingly incorporating agentic AI components into their hacking tools, researchers from Cisco Talos shared an open-source framework on Monday that they hope will be used widely to classify and analyze AI-integrated malware. They also have proof that it's already working.

They're calling the framework Cognitive Artifact Intelligence Research Network, or CAIRN, named after the stacks of stones that hikers set up on trails to mark the path or emphasize something about a certain spot. As malware authors expand their use of AI services, Cisco Talos researchers have used CAIRN to identify a hacking tool with fully autonomous command-and-control infrastructure. Dubbed CLOSEDQUORUM, the malware plotted its moves within a target system by polling up to four large language models (LLMs) about what it should do and taking its directives from that hive mind.

highlights.title: Big tech says AI can find a cure for cancer. So where is it?
highlights.summary: Alongside warnings about its ability to destroy humanity, artificial intelligence is also hailed for its potential to revolutionise health treatment. Just how far can it take us? Her name was June. June would be the last month she ever knew.
body: I remember the way her bed made her so small, swallowed her up in the middle of the room, turned as it was to face the window. With her liver failing, her skin was a ghostly apricot. June – I called her Nan – had been stalked by the king of terrors, the emperor of all maladies: cancer. That son of a bitch.

The cancer was in her pancreas. Odds of survival? “Not good” – putting it lightly. The maths, putting it darkly: it’s the 12th most common cancer worldwide, the sixth most common cause of cancer death. The World Health Organization says it is “one of the cancer types with the least favourable prognosis”. It was not favourable for my grandmother.

The studio confirmed the news in an announcement of its own, confirming that it is now a completely "independent, employee-owned game development studio."

"We're enormously grateful for our years as part of XBOX and for everything that relationship has made possible," says Philip Holt, Studio Head of Undead Labs. "Microsoft has been part of the State of Decay story from the very beginning, and we’re proud of everything we’ve accomplished together."

Undead Labs was just one of several studios that Microsoft has offloaded in recent months, with Double Fine and Compulsion Games similarly finding futures away from the Xbox publishing arm. Ninja Theory has been less successful; however, the studio now on the brink of closure.

highlights.title: Mexican soccer banned promotion and relegation. Senators may bring it back
highlights.summary: Mexican leagues stopped pro/rel in 2020 due to Covid-19. Promised return in 2025 has not materialized. The debate over the absence of promotion and relegation in Mexican soccer has reached the floor of the country’s Senate, where officials announced that a legislative reform to restore the system…
body: Senator Clemente Castañeda of the Movimiento Ciudadano party put forward the proposal, backed by representatives from other party leaderships, including Ignacio Mier of the ruling Morena party.

Castañeda stated that the initiative is critical for “expressly incorporating sporting merit among the obligations that national sports associations must observe” and ensuring promotion and relegation are enshrined in Mexican law.

“When they closed off the possibility of promotion, they didn’t just change a sporting rule; they also restricted a path for players, staff, and sports projects to grow in a country that needs to open up opportunities,” Castañeda said.
The senator said that she invited the president of the Liga MX, Francisco Iturbide, and the commissioner of the Mexican football, Mikel Arriola, and they declined.

highlights.title: A New Chatbot Wants to Unlock the Secrets in Tattered Ancient Greek Records
highlights.summary: In the hope of uncovering new details about ancient life, researchers have developed a large language model that fills in the gaps in papyrus fragments.
body: Academic libraries across the globe are stuffed with hundreds of thousands of Ancient Greek papyrus fragments. Though many are so damaged that their meaning is probably lost, scholars have the ability to restore the rest by methodically filling in missing words or phrases. To accelerate that laborious task, researchers have turned to artificial intelligence.

On Wednesday, the Austrian Academy of Science will release “the world’s first advanced large language model for Ancient Greek,” developed in partnership with French AI lab Mistral and technology services firm Sail Reply. The model, Apollo, is trained on roughly 600 million historical Greek words drawn from manuscripts, papyri, and inscriptions.

The model will be freely available to academics through a chatbot interface. The ambition is to help scholars to more rapidly identify papyrus fragments relevant to their specific sub-disciplines, as well as promising new avenues of research. Where documents are tattered and torn, Apollo is built to fill in the blanks with the most statistically likely words or passages, potentially revealing hidden details about historical events and practices.

highlights.title: Great Britain exit Billie Jean King Cup to mighty Czechia in quarter-finals
highlights.summary: Defeats for Kartal and Boulter condemn Britain to loss. Men will play Germany in quarter-finals of Davis Cup. Great Britain’s stay at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals lasted only one match as they fell to Czechia in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen.
body: Led by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the whole Czech team is ranked higher than any of Britain’s players, and it was Noskova who sealed victory with a 6-2, 7-6 (3) win over Boulter. That followed a lengthy struggle between Marie Bouzkova and Kartal lasting a minute short of three hours, which the Czech eventually took 7-6 (2) 4-6 6-4.

It was a fine effort from Kartal, who was playing her first match in six months after suffering a stress fracture in her back in Indian Wells in March and she will now hope to finish the season strongly. The Czechs will bid for their seventh title in the competition since 2011 while Britain’s hopes of lifting the trophy for the first time are over for another year.

Keothavong’s team have over-performed in the Billie Jean King Cup in recent years and did so again by reaching the finals, with an under-strength team upsetting Australia in April. Neither Kartal nor Boulter were available for that tie, with the former in the early stages of an injury break that would eventually see her miss the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.

Fans don’t just want to watch KPop Demon Hunters, they want to live in the world of HUNTR/X. highlights.title: As a ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Pro, Rylee Arnold Is Making Her Mark
highlights.summary: Ahead of Viral Hits Night, Rylee chats with The Hollywood Reporter about her journey from ‘Juniors’ to the main show, and what she’s learned in her last four years as a ‘DWTS’ pro.
body: Rylee Arnold was destined to become a Dancing With the Stars professional dancer. Having been on the cast for four years now, she’s learned a lot about herself.

Rylee’s older sister, Lindsay Arnold, appeared on DWTS as a pro for 11 seasons, winning season 25 with Jordan Fisher in 2017. One year later, Rylee joined the show’s family alongside her sibling on Dancing With the Stars: Juniors, the spinoff that spotlighted younger stars and dancers.

“I feel like looking back at that time, I was a completely different person,” she says. “But I also love that Rylee so much, because I feel like she went through a lot and she learned a lot about herself. And because of that, I’m here now.”

Fast forward a few years, and Rylee has undoubtedly contributed to the show’s resurgence, by becoming the first pro to utilize social media to garner fan attention and also entice a younger audience to watch. And that intrigue hasn’t slowed down; if anything, it’s rising as each new episode comes out, and as the DWTS pros and celebrities post new pieces of content, inviting audiences into their world.
